title: EU FinServ quantized-model economics probe and procurement triggers
creator: Rajat Verma
description: Objective: Run a targeted market-research and empirical probe to quantify unit-cost, latency, and QA regressions for candidate quantized model variants in EU financial services (FinServ) workloads. Rationale: Enterprise FinServ customers are highly sensitive to both latency and cryptographic/data residency requirements. Quantized models promise cost savings but introduce potential regressions and hardware compatibility variability across cloud regions and on-prem SKUs. Scope: 1) Select 3 representative FinServ workloads (document ingestion summarization, KYC extraction, regulated-chat RAG) and prepare canonical prompt sets sensitive to hallucination and PII redaction. 2) Evaluate 4 model variants: base FP16 open model, 8-bit quantized variant (per-vendor), 4-bit experimental quantized, and a Redwood-verified low-latency variant. 3) Run regional experiments in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 and a VPC-onprem simulated environment. 4) Produce a procurement trigger matrix mapping cost savings to acceptable QA delta and latency SLO impact. Hypotheses: H1: 8-bit quant yields >40% token-cost savings with <3% QA delta on extractive tasks. H2: 4-bit quant shows higher variability across hardware; in EU on-prem it will require kernel fallbacks. H3: Procurement triggers can be automated when latency degradation <10ms and QA delta <2% on canonical tests. Deliverables: experiment workbook, procurement trigger matrix, recommendation memo for sales/solutions, datasets + scripts for reproduction. Methodology: use Redwood Optimize bench harness, deterministic seeds for stochastic tests, side-by-side human labeling sample (n=300 per workload) for QA delta, token-level cost accounting via Console usage export. Success metric: actionable procurement trigger that reduces monthly unit-cost by at least 25% for a defined FinServ workload while keeping customer-facing QA regressions <2% and latency within contractual SLOs.
